items.q: Many long-term backpackers pride themselves on being ______, stretching a modest budget over months on the road without ever feeling deprived.
items.vi: Nhiều người đi du lịch bụi dài ngày tự hào vì mình tiết kiệm, kéo dài một ngân sách khiêm tốn qua nhiều tháng trên đường mà chưa bao giờ thấy thiếu thốn.
items.explanation: Word choice: the clue pride themselves on needs an approving word, and thrifty = spending carefully and wisely, a virtue. ✗ stingy — meanly unwilling to spend, an insult, not a point of pride; ✗ miserly — hoarding money like a miser, also an insult; ✗ tight-fisted — refusing to part with money, again disapproving, and the sentence says the backpackers never feel deprived.

items.q: When the exhibition's visitor figures were queried, it was the junior curator who was left to ______, although every decision had been taken far above her.
items.vi: Khi số liệu khách tham quan của triển lãm bị chất vấn, chính cô phụ trách trưng bày trẻ tuổi phải đứng ra gánh trách nhiệm, dù mọi quyết định đều do cấp trên đưa ra.
items.explanation: Idiom: carry the can = take the blame for something others did, which fits every decision had been taken far above her. ✗ carry the day — win the argument or contest, nothing about blame; ✗ carry the torch — keep a cause (or an old love) alive; ✗ carry the weight — bear a heavy load or responsibility, not a fixed idiom for being made the scapegoat.

items.q: Under mounting pressure from residents, the council has ______ strict limits on the number of cruise ships allowed to dock each day.
items.vi: Trước sức ép ngày càng lớn từ cư dân, hội đồng thành phố đã áp đặt giới hạn nghiêm ngặt về số tàu du lịch được phép cập cảng mỗi ngày.
items.explanation: Collocation: a council imposes limits, rules, fines or taxes on people, and the clue strict limits is exactly what impose takes. ✗ installed — collocates with equipment, software or an official, not limits; ✗ inflicted — you inflict pain, damage or a defeat, not a rule; ✗ instilled — you instil values, fear or confidence in a person, not a numerical cap on ships.

items.q: Visitors from a single neighbouring country ______ nearly half of all overnight stays recorded in the province last year.
items.vi: Du khách từ một nước láng giềng duy nhất chiếm gần một nửa tổng số đêm lưu trú được ghi nhận ở tỉnh này năm ngoái.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: account for = make up a stated share of a total, and the clue nearly half of all overnight stays is a share. ✗ answer for — be held responsible for a fault or crime, so visitors would be being blamed; ✗ allow for — take something into consideration when planning, which needs a person as subject; ✗ stand for — represent or tolerate, neither of which works with a percentage.

items.q: Only when the last tour bus has pulled away ______ the village square return to its usual silence.
items.vi: Chỉ khi chiếc xe du lịch cuối cùng đã rời đi, quảng trường làng mới trở lại sự tĩnh lặng thường ngày.
items.explanation: Inversion: after a fronted Only when… clause the main clause inverts with an auxiliary, and the singular subject the village square plus the present-habit clue has pulled away give does the square return. ✗ do — plural auxiliary, but the subject is singular; ✗ did — past tense, but the time clause is present perfect describing a routine; ✗ has — would need a past participle (returned), not the base form return.

items.q: Reviewers described the resort's manager as ______, brushing aside complaints about the flooded rooms with a shrug and a joke.
items.vi: Người đánh giá mô tả quản lý khu nghỉ dưỡng là kẻ thờ ơ, gạt phăng những lời phàn nàn về các phòng bị ngập bằng cái nhún vai và một câu đùa.
items.explanation: Word choice: indifferent = not caring at all, which matches the clue brushing aside complaints with a shrug. ✗ impartial — fair, not favouring either side, a virtue in a judge, not a fault in a manager; ✗ disinterested — having no personal stake, so able to judge fairly, again a good quality; ✗ unbiased — free from prejudice, also praise, and none of the three describe ignoring flooded rooms.

items.q: The tribunal recommended that the operator ______ every guide in emergency first aid before the trekking season resumes.
items.vi: Hội đồng xét xử khuyến nghị nhà điều hành đào tạo sơ cứu khẩn cấp cho mọi hướng dẫn viên trước khi mùa leo núi bắt đầu lại.
items.explanation: Subjunctive: after recommend / suggest / insist that the verb takes the base-form subjunctive, so that the operator train, with no -s even for a singular subject. ✗ trains — ordinary present tense, but the that-clause after recommended is a proposal, not a fact; ✗ trained — past tense would report what already happened, yet the training is still to come before the season resumes; ✗ would train — would is not used in the subjunctive clause after recommend.

items.q: Scholars who explain the missing layer by an earthquake that no chronicle records are merely ______, the reviewer argued.
items.vi: Những học giả giải thích tầng địa chất bị thiếu bằng một trận động đất mà không biên niên sử nào ghi lại chỉ đang bám víu vào hy vọng mong manh, nhà phê bình lập luận.
items.explanation: Idiom: clutch at straws = rely on a hopeless explanation because nothing better exists, and the clue is an earthquake that no chronicle records, evidence-free guesswork. ✗ splitting hairs — arguing over tiny, unimportant differences; ✗ beating about the bush — avoiding the main point, talking indirectly; ✗ sitting on the fence — refusing to take sides, whereas these scholars have firmly chosen a theory.

items.q: Reluctant to ______ corners on safety, the operator insisted that every raft ______ inspected before the river reopened to tourists.
items.vi: Không muốn làm ẩu về an toàn, nhà điều hành yêu cầu mọi chiếc bè phải được kiểm tra trước khi con sông mở cửa lại cho du khách.
items.explanation: Double blank: the idiom is cut corners = do a job cheaply and carelessly, and insisted that takes the base-form subjunctive be inspected. ✗ clip / be — clip corners is not the idiom, even though the second half is right; ✗ cut / to be — after insisted that every raft a to-infinitive cannot follow the subject; ✗ trim / being — trim corners is not the idiom, and being gives the that-clause no finite verb.

items.q: ______ the lure of overseas travel, most trips taken in the region are still to places within three hours' drive of home.
items.vi: Bất chấp sức hút của du lịch nước ngoài, phần lớn các chuyến đi trong khu vực vẫn là tới những nơi cách nhà không quá ba giờ lái xe.
items.explanation: Linking word: the blank is followed by a noun phrase, the lure of overseas travel, so it needs a preposition, and notwithstanding = despite. ✗ Nevertheless — an adverb that joins two sentences; it cannot govern a noun; ✗ Whereas — a conjunction contrasting two full clauses, but here there is no verb after it; ✗ Albeit — means although and introduces an adjective or reduced clause (albeit slowly), not a noun phrase.

items.q: The dig director was ______ to a fault, insisting that every shard be photographed in place before anyone lifted it.
items.vi: Người chỉ đạo khai quật cẩn trọng đến mức thái quá, yêu cầu mọi mảnh gốm phải được chụp ảnh tại chỗ trước khi ai đó nhấc lên.
items.explanation: Word choice: scrupulous = extremely careful and exact, and the clue insisting that every shard be photographed in place shows that care; to a fault means excessively so. ✗ unscrupulous — without morals, willing to cheat, the opposite idea; ✗ sceptical — doubting or unconvinced, nothing to do with careful method; ✗ secretive — hiding information, but the director is documenting everything.

items.q: The pottery ______ locally, since its clay contains minerals found nowhere in the valley.
items.vi: Số gốm này không thể được làm tại địa phương, vì đất sét của nó chứa những khoáng chất không hề có trong thung lũng.
items.explanation: Modal deduction: can't have + past participle = a confident conclusion that something was impossible, and the clue minerals found nowhere in the valley is the proof. ✗ needn't have been made — it was made but that was unnecessary, not a deduction; ✗ mustn't have been made — mustn't expresses prohibition, not impossibility; the negative deduction is can't; ✗ shouldn't have been made — it was wrong to make it, a criticism rather than a conclusion about origin.

items.q: The traveller's timeline simply does not ______: she claims to have crossed the border twice in a single afternoon.
items.vi: Mốc thời gian của nữ du khách đơn giản là không hợp lý: cô ta khai đã qua biên giới hai lần chỉ trong một buổi chiều.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: add up (intransitive) = make sense, be consistent, and the clue crossed the border twice in a single afternoon is a claim that does not make sense. ✗ add on — attach something extra (a fee, a room), needs an object; ✗ add in — include an item in a total, also needs an object; ✗ sum up — summarise or give the main points, a different meaning entirely.

items.q: The hoard of foreign coins ______ new light on trade routes that no written source ever mentions.
items.vi: Kho tiền xu nước ngoài đã làm sáng tỏ thêm những tuyến thương mại mà không tài liệu thành văn nào từng nhắc tới.
items.explanation: Collocation: the fixed phrase is shed light on = make something clearer, and the clue trade routes that no source mentions shows the coins are revealing information. ✗ pours — you pour a liquid or money into something; pour light on is not the idiom; ✗ spreads — news, disease or butter spreads; ✗ spills — liquid spills; neither collocates with light on in the sense of explaining.

items.q: Tension over overcrowding on the island finally ______ last August, when residents blockaded the ferry terminal.
items.vi: Căng thẳng về tình trạng quá tải trên đảo cuối cùng đã lên đến đỉnh điểm vào tháng Tám năm ngoái, khi cư dân phong toả bến phà.
items.explanation: Idiom: come to a head = reach a crisis point that forces action, and the clue residents blockaded the ferry terminal is that crisis. ✗ came to light — became known or was discovered, but the overcrowding was already obvious; ✗ came to grief — failed badly or had an accident; ✗ came to nothing — produced no result, the opposite of a blockade.

items.q: ______ twice about the unstable slope, the mining company nevertheless pressed ahead with blasting directly beneath the village.
items.vi: Dù đã hai lần bị cảnh báo về sườn dốc không ổn định, công ty khai mỏ vẫn tiếp tục cho nổ mìn ngay bên dưới ngôi làng.
items.explanation: Participle clause: the company received the warnings (passive) and did so before pressing ahead (perfect), so Having been warned is the perfect passive. ✗ Having warned — active, would make the company give the warning to someone else; ✗ Warning — active and simultaneous, so the company would be issuing warnings while blasting; ✗ Being warned — passive but not perfect, so it does not show the two warnings came earlier, and twice demands completed past events.

items.q: Psychologists find that ______ colleagues, who voice the objections others keep to themselves, are often valued more than they are liked.
items.vi: Các nhà tâm lý học nhận thấy những đồng nghiệp thẳng thắn, người nói ra những phản đối mà người khác giữ trong lòng, thường được coi trọng hơn là được yêu mến.
items.explanation: Word choice: outspoken = saying frankly what you think, and the relative clause who voice the objections others keep to themselves defines exactly that. ✗ outstanding — excellent, exceptionally good, says nothing about speaking up; ✗ outgoing — sociable and friendly, not the same as frank; ✗ outlandish — strange or bizarre, which does not fit the neutral tone.

items.q: It is high time the ministry ______ how many visitors the caves can safely absorb in a day.
items.vi: Đã đến lúc bộ phải quyết định các hang động có thể tiếp nhận an toàn bao nhiêu du khách mỗi ngày.
items.explanation: Subjunctive: after It is high time the verb takes the past subjunctive, so decided, even though it refers to the present and means the action is overdue. ✗ decides — present simple is not used after high time; ✗ decide — the base form belongs after recommend / suggest that, not after high time; ✗ will decide — a future tense contradicts the point that the decision should already have been made.

items.q: After one bad experience, the group would sooner ______ the night on the bus than trust another roadside hotel.
items.vi: Sau một trải nghiệm tồi tệ, cả nhóm thà qua đêm trên xe còn hơn tin thêm một khách sạn ven đường nào nữa.
items.explanation: Verb pattern: would sooner / would rather is followed by the bare infinitive, and the clue than trust (also bare) confirms the parallel: would sooner spend. ✗ spending — a gerund cannot follow the modal phrase would sooner; ✗ to spend — to is dropped after would sooner / would rather; ✗ spent — the past form is used only with a different subject (would sooner they spent), not with the same subject.

items.q: ______ evidence survives of the ancient harbour suggests that it silted up within a single century.
items.vi: Chút ít bằng chứng còn sót lại về thương cảng cổ cho thấy nó đã bị bồi lấp chỉ trong vòng một thế kỷ.
items.explanation: Quantifier: What little evidence survives = the small amount of evidence that survives, and the whole phrase is the subject of suggests. ✗ The few — evidence is uncountable, so few cannot modify it; ✗ A little — A little evidence survives would be a complete sentence, leaving suggests without a subject; ✗ Little of — little of must be followed by the (little of the evidence), and again suggests would have no subject.

items.q: Guides will cheerfully embellish a castle's ghost story, but most ______ inventing a massacre that never took place.
items.vi: Hướng dẫn viên sẵn sàng thêu dệt chuyện ma ở lâu đài, nhưng phần lớn dứt khoát không bịa ra một vụ thảm sát chưa từng xảy ra.
items.explanation: Idiom: draw the line at = refuse to go as far as something, and the contrast will cheerfully embellish… but shows the guides set a limit. ✗ draw a veil over — deliberately keep something quiet, hide it; ✗ draw a bead on — aim a gun at a target; ✗ draw a blank on — fail to find or remember something, none of which express refusal.

items.q: ______ the volunteer divers who map the reef every spring, nobody would know how quickly the coral is disappearing.
items.vi: Nếu không có những thợ lặn tình nguyện lập bản đồ rạn san hô mỗi mùa xuân, sẽ chẳng ai biết san hô đang biến mất nhanh đến mức nào.
items.explanation: Inversion: Were it not for + noun inverts If it were not for, and the present result nobody would know marks a present unreal condition. ✗ Had it not been for — past unreal, needs a past result (would have known); ✗ Should it not be for — Should inversion replaces if in future conditions and never combines with be for; ✗ Were it not — the noun the volunteer divers requires for.

items.q: Later digs ______ her hunch: a second gateway was found exactly ______ she had predicted it would be.
items.vi: Những đợt khai quật sau đó đã chứng thực linh cảm của bà: cổng thứ hai được tìm thấy đúng nơi bà đã dự đoán.
items.explanation: Double blank: bear out = confirm a claim, and exactly where she had predicted shows the hunch was proved; the second blank needs the place word where after found exactly. ✗ bore up / where — bear up = stay strong under pressure; ✗ bore out / which — which needs a noun to refer to, so found exactly which is ungrammatical; ✗ bore with / that — bear with = be patient with someone, and that cannot mean in the place that.

items.q: The chronicle portrays the emperor as a ______ ruler who taxed his provinces into ruin to pay for a single palace.
items.vi: Biên niên sử khắc hoạ vị hoàng đế như một kẻ hoang phí, đánh thuế các tỉnh đến kiệt quệ chỉ để xây một cung điện.
items.explanation: Word choice: profligate = recklessly wasteful with money, and the clue taxed his provinces into ruin to pay for a single palace is exactly that. ✗ proficient — skilled and competent, praise rather than criticism; ✗ profound — deep or serious in thought; ✗ prolific — producing a great deal (of books, goals, children), not spending a great deal.

items.q: Although they hold no formal office, the island's fishing cooperatives still ______ considerable influence over how the marine reserve is policed.
items.vi: Dù không nắm giữ chức vụ chính thức nào, các hợp tác xã ngư dân trên đảo vẫn có ảnh hưởng đáng kể tới cách khu bảo tồn biển được giám sát.
items.explanation: Collocation: the fixed pairing is wield influence / power / authority = hold and use it, and the clue considerable influence over how the reserve is policed needs that verb. ✗ brandish — wave a weapon threateningly, so it takes a sword or knife, not influence; ✗ flex — you flex your muscles (literally or figuratively), not influence; ✗ swing — you swing a bat or an axe; swing influence is not English.
